title: A published chapter that runs on your computer
text: This is a proof of concept for publishing a normal .qmd chapter with active R chunks. The page itself is static and hosted on GitHub Pages. When you press Run, the visible code executes in the R installation on your computer and the fresh result returns to this page.

title: A published chapter that runs on your computer
text:
Run locally
Install the current CarmaR app once. Then press Run on my computer or any chunk’s Run button. The browser may ask once whether this site may connect to software on your local network; choose Allow.
CarmaR starts without a helper tab and the status above the chunks changes to CarmaR connected. Nothing executes until you press Run.

title: A published chapter that runs on your computer
text:
1. Create a dataset
This first chunk creates data in your local R session. The code is editable; change it directly before running if you wish.

set.seed(2026)
study <- data.frame(
  learner = paste0("L", 1:12),
  group = rep(c("practice", "comparison"), each = 6),
  score_before = round(rnorm(12, 62, 7), 1)
)
study$score_after <- round(
  study$score_before + ifelse(study$group == "practice", 9, 3) + rnorm(12, 0, 2),
  1
)
study

title: A published chapter that runs on your computer
section: 2. Continue in the same R session
text:
2. Continue in the same R session
Cells share state. This chunk uses study, which was created above.

aggregate(
  cbind(score_before, score_after) ~ group,
  data = study,
  FUN = mean
)

title: A published chapter that runs on your computer
text:
3. Produce a real local plot
The PNG is drawn by your installed R—not by JavaScript or webR—and returned to the published chapter.

cols <- ifelse(study$group == "practice", "#2859c5", "#e28a2b")
plot(
  study$score_before,
  study$score_after,
  pch = 19,
  col = cols,
  xlab = "Score before",
  ylab = "Score after",
  main = "Learning gains"
)
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "grey50")
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend = c("Practice", "Comparison"),
  col = c("#2859c5", "#e28a2b"),
  pch = 19,
  bty = "n"
)

title: A published chapter that runs on your computer
section: 4. Fit a model with base R
text:
4. Fit a model with base R
No optional packages are needed for this proof.

fit <- lm(score_after ~ score_before + group, data = study)
coef(summary(fit))

title: A published chapter that runs on your computer
text:
What this proves

The source remains an ordinary Quarto .qmd file.
The published result remains static HTML suitable for GitHub Pages.
Every visible R chunk becomes a real CarmaR editor with Run and Stop.
Cells execute sequentially in one local R session.
CarmaR’s console, data-frame, plot, and export components render inline.
The native app authorizes only this exact publishing origin for this session.
No extension, helper tab, AI panel, or per-chunk permission is involved.

R code is not sandboxed: inspect unfamiliar chunks before running them.
